# `md/no-empty-link-text`

**A Markdown link has text**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-data` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-data` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | Markdown |
| **Turned on by** | no preset — name it in `[rules]` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `manual` — no automatic fix; the steps are under *How to fix* (the link's text says where it goes, which only the author can write) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-unicorn/no-empty-link-text` |

## What it checks

An inline link whose label is empty or only spaces — `[](https://example.com)`, `[   ](…)` — gives a screen reader nothing to announce and a reader nothing to click. Upstream also treats an image with empty alternative text as an empty label; that is `md/no-alt-text`'s, and not reported here. `md/no-empty-links` checks the destination.

**Why:** A link with no text is invisible or meaningless to anyone not reading the URL.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-data
pip install codelaw-rules-data
```

**No preset turns it on.** Load its pack through any preset (`codelaw:md/recommended` here), then name the rule in `[rules]`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:md/recommended"]

[rules]
"md/no-empty-link-text" = "error"
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"md/no-empty-link-text" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — a scope of your own needs `files`:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.md"]
rules = { "md/no-empty-link-text" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"md/no-empty-link-text" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"md/no-empty-link-text" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"md/no-empty-link-text" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "md/no-empty-link-text": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **Markdown:** `<!-- codelaw-ignore md/no-empty-link-text: <reason> -->`
- **Dated:** `<!-- codelaw-ignore md/no-empty-link-text expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason> -->`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule md/no-empty-link-text --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain md/no-empty-link-text       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule md/no-empty-link-text  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>         # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Write the label between the brackets: `[the release notes](https://example.com)`.

## Examples

### Markdown

#### Don't

```md
See [](https://example.com/notes).
```

#### Do

```md
See [the release notes](https://example.com/notes).
```
